# Toma’s AI voice agents have taken off at car dealerships — and attracted funding from a16z

 Sean O'Kane 

6:00 AM PDT · June 5, 2025
...
Seema Amble, a partner at a16z who led the $17 million that Toma has raised to date, said the pair were “effectively living at these dealerships, going to these dealers’ family barbecues, really understanding how they operate.”
...
Along with a16z, Pamecha and Krivonos attracted investment from Y Combinator (they created Toma at YC in January 2024), the Scale Angels Fund, and auto industry influencer Yossi Levi, also known as the Car Dealership Guy.
...
The Series A “comes at a great time” for Toma, according to Pamecha. The startup only hired its first true sales employee within the last few weeks. Before that, it was still largely Pamecha and Krivonos hustling like they did across the country last summer. 

Without that trip, though, Pamecha said he’s not sure Toma would have reached this point.

Toma, an AI voice startup, has secured $17 million in Series A funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The funding will accelerate Toma's growth and expansion of its voice agents, already deployed in over 100 dealerships. This comes at a pivotal moment, highlighting the demand for AI solutions in the automotive industry. The company's focus on client needs has driven rapid growth and investor interest.
...
Toma is an AI voice startup focused on revolutionizing car dealership operations through the deployment of AI-powered voice agents. Founded in early 2024, Toma's agents handle tasks such as scheduling appointments and processing orders. The company operates on a subscription-based business model and has already established a presence in over 100 dealerships across the nation. Their hands-on experience in the automotive industry has fueled rapid growth and attracted considerable investment.
